tips.comment: Analogical heads to Redcar today after a decisive win at Beverley six days ago on his handicap debut. He carries a 6lb penalty but still looks well-in under a mark of 63. The step up to 1m6f should suit, and with Luke Morris booked again, he’s got a strong chance of following up.

A tentative each way is chanced upon handicap debutante Jedhi Knight, who although hasn't shown much except greenness to date in all of his three starts, all of which were at triple-figure odds. He didn't appear unduly pushed in those races and goes markedly up in trip today which should suit his pedigree.

Cadarn comes into this off a tidy win over course and distance last month, travelling smoothly and finding plenty late on. He’s only up 3lb for that and still looks well-handicapped so should have a solid shot at going back-to-back.

Early Release has been knocking on the door lately, finishing second in two of his last three starts, including a narrow defeat at Windsor two weeks ago. He’s back on turf today and has Billy Loughnane taking over in the saddle. If he can replicate his recent form, he’s got a solid shot at getting his head in front.

Consistent performer at this distance and has won at 5f. Tends to make the places at this level and dropped 1lb for latest 4th when he missed the break. Has claims on previous form and should make top three.

Can excuse last outing where she reared badly in the stalls at the start and lost around 10 lengths before the race developed. The run prior to that was a nice 2nd, losing by just over a length. This is the filly's first run on turf this season, so she is fairly unexposed. She has a great chance to run a big race here, off a handy mark with a plum draw. Talented jockey also claiming 3lbs.
In decent form having won two of his last four races. Hit trouble in running when runner-up at Catterick last time out but can make amends here.

This horse was only beaten a length on debut for a new stable last time out, and the trainer's horses are actually going better now than the bare stats would suggest. The filly has been racing mainly on the AW, but her only win was on the fastest ground she has raced on, so today's conditions should be ideal. The same (excellent) jockey as last time is used again for just the second time, and she looks to be on a winnable mark.

Papa Cocktail is on a dangerous mark now and looks set for his first win since joining the M Herrington stable. He's a 3-time distance winner, and with the trainer in good form, he looks nailed on for at least a place.

Not the force of younger days, the much-raced 11-year-old veteran Musicka (W17, P31 from 128) looks on a handy mark of a career-low 67 today. Taking into account Ben Robinson's stats of 1 win and 5 places from 9 rides, I think an e.w. is worth chancing upon.
Improved on a poor debut to finish second over 5f at Leicester nine days ago. Step up in trip should suit. Should be thereabouts. NAP
Was a promising 5th on debut at Thirsk last time out. Was staying on late that day, so this longer trip will suit. Improvement expected and good chance at good odds.

Ollie Pears generally has most of his two-year-olds ready to do themselves justice on their first runs. So, hopefully, that will be the case with Carnation Queen. Looking at those that have some racecourse experience, there doesn't look to be anything special in the race, which I hope means this newcomer can find a place at least.

Ran well to win over 1m here last month and finished just outside the places in fourth over the same track and trip a fortnight later before finishing runner up over the same trip at Ripon ten days ago. Should be thereabouts.
Unsuccessful over eight furlongs last time out but this looks much more like it for DOVEY MOON and from the same mark of the last trip over this distance, he could well be in the shake up.

A very poor-looking handicap where Yorkshire Myth appeals at a big-looking 16/1. He wasn't beaten far on his handicap debut, which was a step up on previous form. Racing off a lower mark, he can step up on that to be involved here.

I think going down in trip will make life a little easier. He did do well here over C&D when a useful 3rd of 10 last July. So I think he will welcome a return to turf, which is helped by the dropped mark.

Wasn't beaten far when finishing just outside the places in fifth over today's trip at Doncaster sixteen days ago when returning from almost eight months off. Had wind surgery during the break. Won one and placed in four of his six starts before the break. Should be thereabouts.

Cuban Storm did not return well from the break last month and was at the back of the pack. But he will be all the better for that run, and as a result of that finish, he is now back at his last winning mark and worth an EW chance.

Trojan Sun heads to Carlisle today after a solid win at Musselburgh over 1m6f earlier this month. He carries a 4lb penalty but remains on a competitive mark of 60. With proven form over the trip, he looks well-placed to follow up if he maintains his current form.

Back below winning mark, has confirmed running to form in last two starts but seemingly held up too far back to make up ground. A more prominent ride at a trip which suits should see him much harder to beat. Fast ground a plus.

The model I run suggests Bamboo Bay can cause an upset here, and 19s looks like great value, where each way play is a viable value option if that is your preferred betting style. Bamboo Bay lines up with the highest RPR of this field but has the lowest official ranking. This subsequently means he goes out carrying the lowest weight of the 8-runner field. A previous distance winner and last ran 14 days ago, so race fitness is not a concern. Rhys Elliot picks up the reins and relieves a further 3 lbs. This takes the total weight differential to a massive 1 stone 2 lbs over this much longer 1m 6f trip. Although statistically a mid draw is advantageous in the short sprints, over longer distances the low draw helps, giving the option to run the rail and cover less ground.

The model I run suggests There's a Chance can win this one. This result has largely been driven by There's a Chance having the highest RPR of this 7-runner field. Most of the horses go out carrying the same weight, with Argentine Tango carrying 6 lbs more for his prior win at Pontefract 19 days ago. A mid-stall draw (between 5-8) is statistically more important over 5f and 6f. There's a Chance is drawn in stall 3, which might be disadvantageous.

A value chance can be taken with Argentine Tango which made a promising debut being runner-up, and improved subsequently winning in last start. It can be expected to overcome the threat of Venetian Sun.

CALL MARGOT could be worth chancing with her champion sprinter sire. She ran with some credit on her debut in a decent enough looking Listed-class Stakes race at the Curragh and sent across to Britain could be a pointer towards what is expected second-up.
She showed some potential LTO when 3 of 6 at Ripon earlier this month. There is clearly room for improvement, which will be required now going up 2 classes, but also helped with a top jockey.

Zapphire ran as well as she was entitled to at Ascot just over a week ago in a Class 2 race where she really just wasn't in the same league as the two smart fillies that finished ahead of her. She's back to her correct level here and has every chance based on her previous form. I think the Musselburgh seasonal debut can be ignored as that race was run at a crawl, which is absolutely not what Zapphire needs to show her best.

Crowns Lady and Zapphire are the ones to be on here. I'm edging towards Crowns Lady though because of her last run at Beverley where she was a decent 2nd with 9st 7lbs on her back. Now with 8st 11lbs on her back now she should go close.

The model I run suggests Vixey can win this one. Vixey has the same RPR as the other 5 runners here but lines up with the lowest weight to carry around this 7f run. Drawn in stall 6 can be helpful here over this distance. Last ran 14 days ago and came first, so comes in good form and can add another here.
Water Of Leith has been running respectably in competitive sprints and now drops into Class 5 company, which should suit. He’s back on turf and if he gets a clean run he could be in the mix.

Opal Storm returns to Carlisle tomorrow in the 15:00 handicap over 5 furlongs, a track and trip where she caused a stir by winning at 66/1 as a 3 year old. Trained by Brian Rothwell and often partnered with 5lb claimer Aiden Brookes, this 4-year-old filly has demonstrated a liking for the stiff finish at Carlisle. 
In her previous victory here, she showcased blistering early pace and tenacity to hold off challengers, indicating her affinity for the course. Since then, she has remained competitive in sprint handicaps, including a solid campaign last season with a win at Beverley over 5f on good to firm ground. 
With conditions expected to be similar and her mark still looking workable, Opal Storm presents as a value bet. Her proven course form and the booking of Brookes, whose claim aids her cause, further bolster her credentials.

Rock Of England looks poised for a bounce-back performance after two below-par efforts that contrast sharply with his promising seasonal return ??' a close-up fourth at Southwell, beaten less than two lengths off a mark of 76. He’s now dropped 6lbs in the weights since that effort, running off a very workable mark of 70.
That rating is significant when you consider he finished second at Beverley last season off 77 on good-to-firm ground ??' the same conditions expected at Carlisle ??' and even boasts a win here off 82, a full 12lbs higher than today. This Class 5 looks much more within reach.
Tactically, the setup should suit him. With three likely pace-setters in this seven-runner field, a strong early gallop is expected ??' perfect for a horse like Rock Of England who prefers to sit off the pace and finish strongly. PJ McDonald takes the ride and has a solid 19% strike rate at Carlisle over the last 5 Seasons.
Good luck! ?

Mostar Dreams lines up at Carlisle today after a solid second at Doncaster last month, just half a length behind the winner over 6f. She’s back at a track where she’s run well before, including a win over 7f last summer. Should have a decent chance if she builds on that recent effort.
Kings Merchant has had a stop-start beginning to the season but improved to a level above this last season. Now, hopefully ready to roll, this Ed Bethell gelding looks too good for this race.

SACRED FALLS took this race last year in fine fashion off a 5lb lower mark. She has returned as a 5 year old mare in better form than ever with a 3rd & a 1st place to her name. She won with a bit in hand at Catterick over this same 6f trip on the same forecast Good to Firm Going. I think she may have even more to offer. For a more detailed write-up please see my X feed.

Not much between King's Merchant and Jonny Concrete, the top weight. The latter has disappointed the last twice and today the trainer applies blinkers. Jonny Concrete is a very consistent owner-bred four-year old who appears to be improving. He won on seasonal return when unfancied and presumably with something to work with. That was a strong race full of older horses and he has justifiably gone up in the weights. However, with race fitness, he is entitled to improve again at a track where he was runner up last May.

Won his first four starts for this yard when returning from a short break in February but was a well beaten fourth over 6f at Pontefract three weeks ago. William Pyle's 3lb claim should come in useful. Drawn well in stall two. Should be involved at the finish.

We were sort of room last time out and she is 2 lbs below the mark she defied when a neck to Aberama Gold and when ahead of Pearl Dor in these conditions. A bit of money had come and she will go close today for the local trainer.
Previous winner at this distance last year and also placed 2nd twice, both off the same mark as today and with the same jockey. Run in April will have blown off the cobwebs and has a decent draw.
She has been falling in the weights since rising following a good win last August at Pontefract and will need to up her game. Nice inside draw and remains a capable sort. Each way bet.

the model I run suggests Harry Palmer can win this race. Harry Palmer lines up with the highest RPR of this 11 runner field but goes out carrying a relatively low weight compared to the others. Second run after a recent wind surgery and tries the blinkers for the first time to aid concentration. High Draw Stall 11 is advantageous over this 7f trip.

The model I run suggests Legend Forever can win this one. This result has been driven by Legend Forever having the second highest RPR of the 11-runner field. Weight differences here are very small, with exception to the top 2 in the weights who carry quite a bit more. Legend Forever is drawn in stall 9 for this shorter 6f trip, and that can be helpful. In a short 5 or 6f dash, you want to avoid the low stalls. The big risk here is the lack of race fitness. Last run 226 days ago, which is a long break.

This unraced son of Dark Angel is trained by Richard Fahey, and cost a lot of money as a yearling. The key with this horse is to watch the betting, because if the money comes then get on! Can't do that here so tipped up in advance in the hope he's well prepped for his debut.

FLAME OF FOREST ran better than the bare result on debut at Doncaster, doing his best work late under tender handling. That race was pretty hot, and I can see him franking the form with a good showing here.

Rising Empire made a very promising debut when 4th of 15 on debut at Leicester last week. The 6 furlongs here should bring plenty of improvement, and with Oisin Murphy booked, he looks the most likely winner.
Ahead Of Fashion had a cracking run last time out when winning at Kempton but was demoted to second for interference and is worth another shot.
Very much caught the eye on debut as a two-year-old at Leicester before again looking as if there was much more to come first time out this term at Haydock.
Daughter of Night of Thunder, who was a well-beaten short-priced favourite on debut at Kempton in December, ran well in a good race on turf debut at Ascot 3 weeks ago. The one to beat this evening.
Trainer Ed Walker has been very complimentary about the 3yo filly Electrifarhh. A daughter of Farhh, Walker thinks she will be capable of black type in the future.

Crowd Quake steps back into action at Windsor after a breakthrough win over this course and distance two weeks ago. That was his first try at 1m2f, and he handled it well, winning by over a length at 11/1. He’s up 6lb for that, but still looks fairly treated off a mark of 51 so should have a solid chance of following up.
Offiahs Boy did a good job getting a close second last time out when second up after wind surgery and worth another go off the same mark

GLEN ESK has shown glimpses of life since returning to the track with blinkers on. His handicap mark has been in freefall, and he returns to a C&D he's performed really well at for his previous handler. Bounce back to form expected at a big price.

Toca Madera has been in the money without winning for two of the three runs this year, with the latest being third. He goes again with the same rider off the same mark, while just 1 lb above his last winning mark.
Talented 6 year old who produced a career best when winning at Newmarket last month. Lost nothing in defeat when 2nd over 6 furlongs here last time and should go very well once again this evening.
Won here this time last year from 1 lb lower with a 7 lb claimer on board. So should be spot on for this 4th run back after a break with a good draw in 1.

Toca Madera can be opposed here given T Jakes’s 3% SR (A/E 0.26) on sole trainer runners that day and the B Meehan yard form (6% SR, A/E 0.4 over the past month). Regal Envoy will do well to overcome awful 7% SR (A/E 0.35) with fancied runners in May, meanwhile Jumbeau carries a poor FlatStats rating alongside Brazen Beau’s damning 9% SR (A/E 0.41) with fancied runners in C1-3 races. S Williams holds a poor 3% SR (A/E 0.29) with J Morley runners which puts the badly FS rated Existent up against it but RHYTHM N HOOVES has shown to be a capable operator on his day and 7/1 is a decent each way price. The 5yo has been busy since December with 2W 1P from 9 starts and plenty of solid efforts along the way. A 1.25l 4th of 7 at Goodwood on turf reappearance earlier this month was a promising sign, particularly given he lost a shoe, and he’s been dropped a pound for that effort so should be competitive again here. Pearl Secret’s 18% SR (A/E 1.67) on pear-shaped tracks and 18% SR (A/E 1.51) over 5f adds further confidence.

Existent arrives in excellent form, having finished runner-up in each of his last three starts. Most recently, he was narrowly denied in a valuable Class 2 at Goodwood, going down by just a neck after hitting the front a furlong from home. That effort earned him a 1lb rise to a mark of 83 ??' still well below his peak, having previously won off 94 on the all-weather.
His penultimate run was another strong second in a competitive Class 3 handicap at Epsom, further confirming his consistency and current fitness. Warren Fentiman, who partnered him in those last two near-misses, retains the ride, and that continuity can only be a plus.
The race setup looks ideal: with confirmed front-runners Twilight Jet and Ziggy’s Missile drawn on either side, there should be a strong pace for Existent to track and pounce late.
Good luck! ?

Things were looking really good when winning at Newmarket in October of 2021 but runs in Ireland has not gone to plan so hoping return to U.K. flats kick starts his career again and is helped by dropping down 4 classes today.

She has struggled for form and consistency since her last win at Nottingham last October. But it helps that she's a C&D winner and with a 5lb claimer, her last winning mark is 3lbs lighter, so she is not one to be underestimated.

Hannon is hitting form at the right time for this girl to get in the winner's enclosure. Much improved last start when chasing home the smart and well-regarded Tycoon. The closing sectionals in that were super impressive as she actually had the best FSP off a crawl pace. She should have more than enough in hand to be winning off 71 in her handicap debut. I think she could wipe the floor with these.
Riyadh Gem won after a break last month and kept on well to the post while just doing enough. This makes me think the step up to 1m3f will suit while keeping Hollie Doyle in the saddle.

A four-time winner when fresh, Lipsink has a course and distance win and also two C&D 2nds under his belt. His last race is best excused as the hood was a bit late coming off at the start, which meant he wasn’t up with the pace and hence was eased once the chance had gone.

Nicely weighted with a good low draw in 3. Just 3 lbs above last winning mark, and his 2 runs so far this season have substance. Finishing behind Candyman Stan, who has won again since, and LTO at Epsom finished one place behind Small Fry, who won impressively at Chester. 2 lbs lower here is a bonus.
Macari won at Salisbury last week on GF in a C3 and drops back to C4 with the same rider. While under penalty for that, I think there could be more improvement today with the same rider in this 0-78.

EDUCATOR is ridden by Hollie Doyle again who sprang a surprise on the all-weather latest. This mature type is an early career turf winner from a higher mark and maybe he can progress from his last and most recent win representing a highly experienced dual-purpose yard.

Trainer and jockey in good form. Set the pace on last run, finished two and a quarter lengths fourth here in April. Probably needed the run as been off since November. Should strip a lot fitter today. Each way NAP.
Xiomara returns to Windsor today after a quiet run at Saint-Cloud last time out. She’s back on British turf and steps up to 1m3f, which might suit her better.

Unfortunately, not among the 5 LTO winners in this field. Makes course debut, and hopefully, it helps that the last win was off a higher mark. But also hoping her temperament is not called into question, as she has refused to race in the past.
Finished second on debut at Chelmsford over distance. George Wood takes the ride today and has a 15% strike rate, +13.43 profit when riding for R. Spencer.

Thrice-raced gelding who gained valuable course experience LTO despite finishing 9th of 12 last month. Now going down in trip, which should make life a little easier. With some improvements, it's worth finding out if he can cause an upset with the current price on offer.

The 12 year old CHEF DE TROUPE has fallen to 4lb below his last winning mark and he has a great record at this time of year especially with a run under his belt. Could outrun his odds. Each way for 4 places at 40/1 advised. See my X feed for a much more detailed write-up.
Got to be worth a go here. Hasn't fired for the new yard, but Carol team will get this one going at some point and a huge price. Maybe look for the late money tomorrow.

Veteran, who returned from 15 months off the track with a really solid course and distance 3rd in March, produced a similar level of form at Chelmsford last time. Something similar this evening should see him bang there once again.

Swiss Ace looks like he could bounce back now returning to his optimum conditions ??' 7 furlongs on the all-weather. His recent runs have come under less-than-ideal circumstances, either on turf or over varying trips, which have kept his mark trending downward. Now rated 67, he’s a full 10lbs below his last winning mark of 77, offering real value on past form.
Last time out, he hinted at a return to form, shaping better than the result suggested ??' a sign that he’s coming to the boil at just the right time. Back over his favoured trip and surface, he takes on weaker opposition here and should get a good toe into the race with an even pace expected.
Harry Davies (14% strike rate at Wolverhampton) is a positive jockey booking, and trainer Ruth Carr has a solid 12% strike rate at the track. With conditions finally in his favour, Swiss Ace could easily outrun his current mark.
Good luck! ???'?

I'm backing Sustained in the 21:00 at Wolverhampton. This 4-year-old gelding, trained by Daniel & Claire Kubler, has shown promise in his early career. Notably, he secured a victory at Wolverhampton over 1m 1f in June 2024, demonstrating his ability to handle the Tapeta surface. His pedigree, being by Inns Of Court out of Pearly Brooks, suggests he possesses both speed and stamina. 
Returning to a Class 5 handicap over 1m 142y after a break, a distance he's proven over, could play to his strengths. With Richard Kingscote taking the ride, the partnership could prove advantageous. 
Given his past performances and the conditions of the race, Sustained presents a solid each-way opportunity in this contest
Has shown some promise in his three maidens to date and looks likely to be suited by this step up in trip. Appears to be on a pretty lenient mark for his handicap debut.
In what looks like being a really open race, I am going to side with The Real Screamer, who has won 2 of the last 4 and was close in the other 2, and could easily land this.

Bright N Shine returns to action in the 19:10 Abbey Hotel Roscommon Handicap (Class 4) at Roscommon, a 1m2f58y contest on good to firm ground. Trained by Terence O'Brien, this 5-year-old gelding by Fulbright carries a rating of 75 into this 17-runner field. 
Notably, Bright N Shine has demonstrated a strong affinity for this distance, securing two wins from three starts over similar trips. His recent form includes a commendable third-place finish in a 1m2f handicap at Navan on April 26, 2025, where he was beaten just over three lengths on soft ground. This performance suggests he remains competitive and capable of making an impact in this field. 
With the going at Roscommon expected to be good to firm, conditions should suit Bright N Shine well. His proven ability over the distance and recent form make him an appealing each-way proposition at likely generous odds.

Divelement ran well when fourth over course and distance on debut a week ago in what looked a fairly decent maiden. Showed a lot of speed at the front end but also saw the race out well when passed, ultimately only beaten two lengths. Looks a play at odds of 6-4 with none of the newcomers here looking especially fancied. James Ryan claims 3lbs again for trainer Jack Davison (SR 17%).
Predominantly a hurdler with two wins and two places from 13, Ragmans Corner makes his fourth flat appearance today with the notable booking of Colin Keane on flat handicap debut.

Ozark Daze is still left searching for that maiden win, but not for the lack of effort. With 2 runner-up finishes as well as another couple of 3rd placed finishes inside the last handful of outings, showing a consistency of performance that will be rewarded sooner rather than later.

MATT CONNOR is a well treated middle-distance handicapper taking his chance for a shrewd dual-purpose yard. He has the benefit of a reappearance sighter behind him now and the booking of classy experienced jockey Billy Lee has potential significance.

Coulstys Way is still a maiden after 7 starts but looks sure to go well based on her two starts this season. 3rd of 12 at Tipperary last month was followed by 2nd of 9 at Ballinrobe 10 days ago. Both of those runs were over 1m1f, but the step up to 1m4f should suit. She is 2 lbs higher but looks a good EW bet with 4 places on offer.

Jack Cleary claims a 5 lbs allowance for Adrian Murray stable here. The 3-year-old filly Alumni Lia is by Derby winner Australia. She has run quite well on the last two starts, third at Dundalk and then ran prominently at Sligo last time over a shorter trip than this. A chance that run 15 days ago will up her fitness. 'Not taken lightly' suggests Timeform. Has a squeak at odds of 16-1 in quite an open-looking 3-year-old handicap.
Up in trip for this run. Good run in third by just over three lengths at Gowran, after interference at the start. Was bumped into, was keeping on in the final furlong. Each way bet today.
